questions.a: Silhouette extent survives coalescing. MEASURED: near [16.75 16.36 28.57] vs far at 2% keep [13.61 15.03 27.85] -- height within 2.5% while splat count falls 48,870 -> 977 (50:1).

At what scale does this feature operate?
questions.a: Horizon scale: tens to hundreds of metres from the anchor. Landmark is 26 m tall and still reads at 200 m.

questions.q: What is the right definition level for this scale?
Could this be decomposed further? Into what?
questions.a: Yes, and it already does: landmark -> 9 tiers -> placed children -> splats. Each tier is a ring of recombined children at decreasing radius.

questions.q: At what resolution does the pattern emerge?
questions.a: The silhouette stops reading below roughly 1,000 splats. MEASURED: 977 splats at 2% keep still holds shape; that is the floor of this rung.

Would training this require GPU acceleration?
questions.a: Yes. Rendering 105k+ splats per frame across tiles plus landmark is GPU-only; measured 442 ms for 6 tiles on the 4090.

questions.q: Does this feature connect to the Mirror of Erised?
How directly does it serve the Mirror? (direct/enabling/orthogonal)
Would a costless life still be meaningful without this feature?
Could this feature be gamed to fake a generous life?
What would this feature look like if it perfectly served the Mirror?
What other features does this compose with?
questions.a: Composes with DOWN (ground tiles) via compose(). Shares world_height() so the base sits on the terrain rather than floating.

questions.q: What could break at the seam between this and its neighbors?
questions.a: The base must sample the SAME world_height() as the tile it stands on, or it floats or sinks. Wired via the relief parameter. Second seam risk: LOD popping between discrete distance bands.

questions.q: Does this need a decoder step to place in the level?
questions.a: Yes. Placed by absolute world coordinate, deterministic -- same place forever. That is the allocentric half of the six-directions rule.

questions.q: What would a failed composition look like?
Does this feature need a human judgment or can the system verify it?
questions.a: System-verifiable for silhouette preservation (extent comparison is a number). NOT system-verifiable for 'does it draw the player onward' -- that needs the human.
